question: Will H.R. 33 (United States–Taiwan Expedited Double-Tax Relief Act) be enacted into law before May 1, 2026?
summary: Ensemble suggests 8% odds; signals higher upside from Senate companion and Treasury negotiations, plus strong House support.
Major downside risk remains Senate inaction by May 1, 2026, and no final presidential action yet as of early 2026.
Threshold-analysis indicates enactment by May 1 is improbable; objections premised on threshold breach carry little weight.
Overall calibration places probability between 8% and 20%, with a point estimate around 12% reflecting mixed momentum and persistent hurdles.

justification.critique_assessment: Objections about Senate delay are valid; they rightly highlight downside risk, but there is also tangible upside from Senate companion momentum and treasury negotiations.
justification.adjustment: Adjusted upward from 0.08 to 0.12 to incorporate the positive signals (Senate companion introduced, House passage, and ongoing treasury talks) while preserving the dominant risk of Senate inaction; did not lower the estimate on threshold-breach concerns.
